texto.@es: La mayoría de los verbos forma el pasado con **-ed**: work → **worked**, play → **played**, visit → **visited**. Si acaba en **-e**, añadimos solo **-d**: dance → **danced**. Si acaba en consonante + **-y**, cambiamos **y** por **i** y añadimos **-ed**: study → **studied**. En algunos verbos de una sílaba que terminan en vocal corta + consonante, doblamos la consonante final: stop → **stopped**.
texto.@en: Most verbs form the past with **-ed**: work → **worked**, play → **played**, visit → **visited**. If you end up in **-e**, we add only **-d**: dance → **danced**. If you end up in consonant + **-y**, we change **y** to **i** and add **-ed**: study → **studied**. In some verbs of a syllable that end in short vowel + consonant, we double the final consonant: stop → **stopped**.

texto.@es: La forma del pasado es igual con todas las personas: **I worked**, **she worked**, **they worked**.
texto.@en: The shape of the past is the same with all people: **I worked**, **she worked**, **they worked**.

texto.@es: La terminación escrita **-ed** tiene tres pronunciaciones: /t/ en **worked**, /d/ en **played** e /ɪd/ en **visited**. Escucha o lee la terminación final; la escritura siempre es **-ed**.
texto.@en: The **-ed** written termination has three pronouncements: / t / in **worked**, / d / in **played** and / or in **visited**. Listen or read the final termination; the writing is always **-ed**.

texto.@es: Usamos **did** en preguntas y **didn't** en negativas. Después, el verbo vuelve a la forma base: **Did you play?**, **I didn't play**; nunca «Did you played?» ni «didn't played».
texto.@en: We use **did** in questions and **didn't** in negatives. Then the verb returns to the base form: **Did you play?**, **I didn't play**; never «Did you played?» or «didn't played».
